## Design Taste
*Source: https://antigravity.google/ — generated by /taste*

### Tokens
- Spacing scale: 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 36 / 48 / 60 / 72 / 80 / 120px (base unit 4px)
- Type scale: hero 80px/450, h2-large 54px/450, h2 42px/450, h2-small 32px/450, lede 24px/450, body 17.5px/400, button 14.5px/450 — single family "Google Sans Flex" for everything
- Colors: background `#F8F9FC`, background-inverse `#121317`, text-primary `#45474D`, text-heading `#121317`, accent `#3279F9` (used on one page only), surface white `#FFFFFF`
- Radius: 9999px (buttons/badges), 36px (large panels), 24px (cards), 16px/8px/4px (small elements)
- Shadows: none — this system uses zero elevation shadows
- Motion: `transform 0.3s ease-in-out, background-color 0.3s` shared hover transition, always eased 0.15-0.3s

### Directives
- When building any clickable element (button, badge, chip), always use fully-rounded `9999px` radius — because this system uses one pill shape for every interactive control regardless of context.
- When choosing depth/elevation for cards or panels, always use a near-invisible background tint (not a shadow) — because this design communicates depth through color-tint and whitespace only.
- When setting type hierarchy, always vary size and the variable-font weight axis (400/450/500) within a single family — because this system never pairs a display font with a separate body font.
- When adding hover/interaction motion, always keep it to `transform`/`background-color` at 0.15-0.3s eased — because functional motion here is deliberately restrained and identical across contexts.
- When introducing an accent color, always confine it to the one screen where it does real work (e.g. a pricing/comparison view) — because this system treats color as scarce and task-specific, not a site-wide brand wash.

### Anti-patterns
- Never add `box-shadow` to cards, panels, or buttons — this system has zero shadows anywhere.
- Never pair a separate display/heading font with the body font — this system uses one variable family for everything.
- Never spread the accent color across nav, headers, or backgrounds — it belongs only where the user is comparing options (e.g. pricing tiers).
- Never use true bold (700) — the heaviest weight observed in this system is 500, with 450 as the dominant "emphasis" weight.
- Never attach decorative/atmospheric animation to functional UI feedback — keep brand-mood motion (particles, background flourishes) separate from interactive hover/click states.
